title: Weight-space programming for tractor guidance controller: large language models natively write neural network weights that steer a real tractor

target_networks.name: 253-parameter tokenised steering network (9-4-4 encoder + 22-8-1 head, tanh)

domain: robotics / agricultural vehicle control (tractor path tracking)
tasks_benchmarks: simulated AMX G-trac path tracking on 512 held-out random paths (objective J)
field test on real AMX G-trac tractor, 2779 m path

headline_result.text: With 25 simulated evaluations, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 each repaired a PPO-trained 253-weight steering network for a slower actuator and wrote a working controller from all-zero weights (J 4.94 and 7.00, no failures on 512 held-out paths), where an evolution strategy found none from zero even with 1000 evaluations; PPO remained more accurate.
headline_result.quote: With simulated feedback, both models repaired the trained network in single sessions and wrote a working controller from zero weights, whereas from zero the evolution strategy found none.

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: single session per model and start point; zero-shot repair 10 repetitions; ES 5 seeds

notes_for_review: A careful engineering case study: equal-budget evolution strategy and gain-grid baselines, PPO references, held-out paths, linearised closed-loop checks of stated vs measured gains, and a real-tractor field run. The task is tiny (253 weights) and the LLM essentially hand-designs a classical cascaded controller with feed-forward inside the network, so it shows LLMs encoding control-engineering knowledge into weights rather than learning; each condition rests on a single session. No code or data release is stated, and the author frames it as a new 'Era 4' / 'Weight-Space Engineering', which is a strong framing for n=1 sessions.
